# An exact continuous minorant for one integer coordinate and constant envelope scale

This proves a restricted nonsmooth payment for the NEW body-tied H cover. It does not cover nonconstant affine envelope scales or arbitrary integer dimension. Unlike the strict-convex outer-contact argument, it does not use surface regularity or any new body variation.

## 1. Exact hypotheses

Let d>=1. Let C be a convex body in R x R^d with finite complete sampled base P. Suppose its actual single H-cover group has a full-base-rank occupied source interval B with an integer relative-interior witness. Suppose the marked homothetic envelope from the full-rank source-face theorem has CONSTANT scale ell>0:

    C_z subset y(z)+ell D,
    C_z = y(z)+ell D for z in B,

where y is affine and D is a d-dimensional convex body with 0 interior. The equality holds at all real bases of B, as proved by the common source-face support theorem. Each sampled fiber is positive-volume. Let M=sum_(z in P)|C_z|.

All selected original mass-Q critical caps of this same physical group propagate over the envelope, so their pointed form is

    H_j^D={xi:u_j·xi+epsilon f_D Gamma(u_j)>=0}.       (1)

Normalize Gamma(u_j)=1. Here f_H(z,y(z))=ell f_D on the source interval and f_D>0. Let P_D(xi)=1+a_D·xi>0 be the actual ordinary projective energy normalizer of (D,0). The group's positive contact weights rho_j, summing to one, satisfy

    sum_j rho_j u_j=epsilon f_D a_D.                 (2)

The same Q is the original mixed volume of every selected cap, not the volume of an auxiliary body. These hypotheses follow for the explicitly constructed H group from `candidate 8effe5eb4947ba88` and the full-rank cap propagation in `candidate 696a6484b3fda438`. They do not follow from parameter-plane compression alone.

## 2. A single actual convex filling

Apply the base-preserving affine change x=y(z)+ell xi. Its common fiber Jacobian is ell^d. The resulting ordinary convex body is

    T={(z,xi):(z,y(z)+ell xi) in C} subset R x D.

For xi in D let

    A_xi={z:(z,xi) in T},
    L(xi)=length(A_xi),
    m(xi)=#(A_xi intersect Z).

Each A_xi is a compact interval containing B. Every integer in B is a source base because the deepest-base hull is lattice-complete. In particular B has integer endpoints and an integer point in its relative interior, so it contains at least three integer points. Therefore m(xi)>=3 for every xi in D.

For ANY compact interval A containing m integers,

    m-1 <= length(A) <= m+1.                        (3)

Indeed its first and last included integers are m-1 apart, while each endpoint lies less than one unit outside them unless it is itself an included integer. The weak displayed bounds include all endpoint conventions; closed endpoint mass only increases m. There is no lattice/general-position approximation here.

The pointed original mixed-volume density is exactly

    f(xi)=ell^d m(xi) 1_D(xi),  integral f=M.         (4)

Because T is convex, its one-dimensional section length L is concave on D: Minkowski inclusion of interval sections gives L((1-t)xi+t eta)>=(1-t)L(xi)+t L(eta). Set

    g(xi)=(3/4) ell^d L(xi) 1_D(xi).                (5)

The body T is compact, so g is bounded and integrable. It is positive on D and has convex support. By (3) and m>=3,

    (3/4)L <= (3/4)(m+1) <= m,
    (3/4)L >= (3/4)(m-1) >= m/2.

Hence the exact POINTWISE inequalities hold:

    f/2 <= g <= f,       integral g >= M/2.         (6)

The density g is concave on its convex support and therefore log-concave. It also has convex g^(-1/b) for every b>0, though that stronger description is not needed.

## 3. The original finite-epsilon menu covers D

There is no need to pass to an epsilon-zero balanced circuit. At every xi in D, (1)--(2) give

    sum_j rho_j [u_j·xi+epsilon f_D]
          =epsilon f_D [1+a_D·xi]
          =epsilon f_D P_D(xi)>0.                   (7)

Thus at least one ORIGINAL pointed cap H_j^D contains xi. This is an actual common-cap cover of all D, retaining its original Q and normals. The positivity of P_D on D is essential; replacing the energy normalizer by an arbitrary affine function would not justify (7).

## 4. Exact critical-mass payment

Use the already proved radial-centering theorem for bounded compact log-concave densities (`candidate faf22898d0dc8331`). It supplies one point c in D such that every closed halfspace containing c has g-mass at least Gamma_d integral g, where Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d. The density g is full-dimensional, bounded and positive on the interior of D, so all hypotheses hold. For d=1 this is also the ordinary weighted-median theorem with Gamma_1=1/2.

By (7) one selected original cap H_j^D contains c. Its actual original mixed cap mass is Q=integral_(H_j^D)f, because the cap factorization holds on every original fiber, not just on the source interval or on the outer boundary. Therefore

    Q = integral_(H_j^D) f
      >= integral_(H_j^D) g
      >= Gamma_d integral g
      >= (Gamma_d/2) M.                             (8)

All halfspaces here are closed. Hyperplanes have zero f- and g-mass because both are bounded d-dimensional densities, but no open/closed replacement is needed. The continuous point c is only used to choose one member of an existing mass-Q cap menu; it is not asserted to be a mixed-integer OC center.

Thus an attained H configuration with the stated one-group/full-rank/constant-scale hypotheses cannot have beta=Q/M below the exact n=1 target Gamma_d/2, even at finite epsilon. The conclusion is valid for nonsmooth D and all d>=1. It leaves nonconstant ell, hollow or lower-rank deepest hulls, and n>=2 unresolved.
